title: FISH AND WILDLIFE POLICY AND GOVERNANCE
description: Examines historical and contemporary policy, law, and governance regarding fish and wildlife in the United States. Addresses key regulatory and procedural aspects essential for the conservation and management of fish and wildlife in both state and federal settings. Introduces and analyzes policy as a social process, exploring the various governance and planning processes that shape how fish and wildlife policies are developed, modified, and implemented.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisite: FW 251.
A minimum grade of D- is required in FW 251.

Enrollment is limited to students with a program in Fish, Wildlife & Conserv Scien (018) or Fisheries & Wildlife Sciences (733).
books_html: No-cost: Course utilizes open educational resources, materials available through the library, or does not require any purchased materials.
clssnotes:
Major restriction extends through Week 10 of registration.
